title: 'Ram-Raid' Leaves Employee Critically Injured, Jewelry Store in Ruins (Video)
text: Headlines ‘Ram-Raid’ Leaves Employee Critically Injured, Jewelry Store in Ruins (Video) Security guard thwarted apparent coordinated heist after a stolen car was crashed into South Sacramento jewelry store. Published 2 days ago on April 24, 2026 By INSTORE Staff Share Tweet A violent “ram-raid” robbery attempt at a South Sacramento, CA, jewelry store left an employee critically injured and a storefront in ruins Saturday afternoon. According to the Sacramento County Sheriff’s Office cited by ABC News, a stolen vehicle was intentionally driven through the storefront of Chinna Jewellers in the 7400 block of Stockton Boulevard at approximately 4:30 p.m. on April 18. Store owner Inderjit Singh described the impact as sounding like an “explosion.” Singh’s uncle, an elderly employee who was inside at the time, was struck and pinned under the vehicle. He remains hospitalized with critical injuries. The attempted heist was thwarted by Alex Marchuk, a private security supervisor, who drew his firearm and confronted a suspect wearing a hoodie and black gloves. As Marchuk pursued the primary suspect, he observed several other vehicles arrive and multiple individuals exit carrying bags, suggesting a highly organized operation. “When they saw me with a gun … they very quickly jumped again inside and they were running from here,” Marchuk told KCRA 3. Edward Igoe of the sheriff’s office credited Marchuk’s intervention with preventing the theft. No merchandise was taken, though Singh reported extensive damage to the store’s security gates and structure. It is the second time the business has been targeted since 2020. Suspects could face charges of attempted robbery and attempted murder. No arrests have been made.
